gaps.sentence: You ___ better take an umbrella; it looks like rain.
Students ___ to buy the textbook; copies are available in the library.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' plus the infinitive expresses absence of obligation: don't have to buy.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not agree, but let us ask him anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'May' expresses a possibility about the future: may not agree.

gaps.sentence: ___ we take the motorway, or will the coast road be quicker?
gaps.explanation: 'Should we ...?' asks for advice or an opinion: Should.

gaps.sentence: When I was a child, I ___ stay up late on New Year's Eve.
gaps.hint: permission that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Was allowed to' expresses past permission; 'could' is also possible: was allowed to.

gaps.sentence: You ___ touch that wire — it carries a live current!
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' signals something absolutely not allowed: mustn't touch.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.
